key_insight: This paper shows that myocardial infarction can be localized from echocardiography by combining motion-conditioned modeling with multi-view fusion, improving the use of weakly supervised cardiac ultrasound data. The key idea is to learn from motion cues across views instead of relying heavily on dense manual annotations.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of localizing myocardial infarction from echocardiography when detailed annotations are scarce. Existing motion-analysis methods often depend on handcrafted features or dense supervision, which limits scalability and real-world deployment.
method: Uses motion-conditioned representations to capture regional wall motion abnormalities in echocardiography.
Fuses information from multiple ultrasound views to improve robustness and localization accuracy.
Leverages weaker forms of supervision and foundation-model-style visual priors to reduce annotation burden.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work demonstrates how motion-aware and multi-view learning can make medical image analysis more practical in low-annotation settings. It offers a promising blueprint for building clinically useful models from widely available but imperfectly labeled data.

paper_title: Motion-Conditioned Multi-View Fusion for Myocardial Infarction Localization from Echocardiography
paper_authors: Guang Yang, Wentian Xu, Siyu Wang, Betty Raman, Lei Li
